editorial:
The Skydivers is a 1963 US feature written and directed by Coleman Francis and produced by Anthony Cardoza. Crown International Pictures distributed it. Wikipedia says it fell into obscurity and found a second life in 1994, when it was the basis for a Mystery Science Theater 3000 episode. A reuser would want it for the MST3K connection, or as an example of Francis's low-budget work.

The rights trap is that this dossier cannot confirm the film's status. A 1963 film is protected for 95 years unless it lost protection through a missing notice or a missing renewal. Renewal was due during 1991, which is year 28 after the 1963 publication. Early filings in 1990 are possible. I could not check the renewal records. Do not treat the film as free to use until someone searches the Copyright Office public records (publicrecords.copyright.gov) for renewals filed in 1990-1991. Add 1992 only as a safety margin. An MST3K version would add riffing and commentary that is separately protected, so it is not a clean copy of the film.
faq: Is The Skydivers (1963) in the public domain?

Not confirmed. Because it was published in 1963, it is public domain only if it lacked a copyright notice or was never renewed. I did not complete the renewal search. Search the Copyright Office public records (publicrecords.copyright.gov) for renewals filed in 1990-1991 (1992 only as a safety margin) before reusing it.
Can I use clips from the MST3K episode of The Skydivers?

Do not assume they are free. The episode's riffing and commentary are separately protected. The episode also contains the film itself, and the film's status is unconfirmed. Whether a particular use is permitted depends on the facts, so get the film's status settled first and use a clean copy of the film.
